newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine call rate eases on C. Bank rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Philippine call rate eases on C. Bank rate cut.

text.p: The Philippine overnight money eased to 16.03125 percent in step with the two percentage point reduction in the Central Bank overnight rates earlier in the day, traders said.
The average interbank call loan was at 18.03125 percent on Wednesday.
Traders lent out money to fellow traders with only a slight premium over the Central Bank's 16.0 percent benchmark rate.
"The banks just went along with the rates of Central Bank," one trader said, adding that the system was still awash with cash.
Turnover was light with only 7.697 billion pesos changing hands.
The secondary Treasury bill rates were slightly lower as banks scrambled for T-bills before rates go down further.
The Central Bank lowered its term reverse repo rates, prompting banks to expect further decline in T-bill rates.
"There were a lot of buyers, but very few sellers. Many bankers want to keep the bills for themselves and their clients," one trader said.
"Activities have died down a little due to absence of sellers," another trader said.
She said banks with excess funds are waiting for Monday's auction to beef up their T-bill inventory.

A survey of seven banks showed the bids for the three-month bills ranged from 10.65 to 10.90 percent, hewing close to the Central Bank's three-month special series bills being offered at 10.6 percent.
